title: Strong monoidal Hom comparison from an exact dual pair
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category], with internal Homs $H_{\mathcal C},H_{\mathcal D}$ specified by natural adjunction bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(A\otimes T,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,H(A,B))$. Let $G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be a strong monoidal functor [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], with tensorator $\mu_{A,B}:GA\otimes GB\xrightarrow{\sim}G(A\otimes B)$. Let $D,P\in\mathcal C$ have maps $e:P\otimes D\to\mathbf1$ and $c:\mathbf1\to D\otimes P$ satisfying $(e\otimes1_P)(1_P\otimes c)=1_P$ and $(1_D\otimes e)(c\otimes1_D)=1_D$, with associators and unitors understood. For every $N\in\mathcal C$, the specified comparison
$$\gamma_{P,N}:G H_{\mathcal C}(P,N)\longrightarrow H_{\mathcal D}(GP,GN),$$
defined as the transpose of $GP\otimes G H_{\mathcal C}(P,N)\xrightarrow{\mu}G(P\otimes H_{\mathcal C}(P,N))\xrightarrow{G(\operatorname{ev})}GN$, is an isomorphism. No equivalence or exactness assumption on $G$ is required.

proof.text:
Write $u:\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}\xrightarrow{\sim}G\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}$ for the unit comparison. Set $e'=u^{-1}\circ G(e)\circ\mu_{P,D}$ and $c'=\mu_{D,P}^{-1}\circ G(c)\circ u$. These are maps $GP\otimes GD\to\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}$ and $\mathbf1_{\mathcal D}\to GD\otimes GP$. Expand either triangle composite using these formulas. Naturality of $\mu$ moves $G(e)$ and $G(c)$ together; associativity coherence changes the two successive tensorators on three factors into the tensorator for the other parenthesization, and unit coherence cancels $u,u^{-1}$ against the unitors. Thus, with precisely the associators and unitors of [def-sfb-monoidal-category] inserted, the two resulting equalities are
$$(e'\otimes1_{GP})(1_{GP}\otimes c')=G\bigl((e\otimes1_P)(1_P\otimes c)\bigr)=1_{GP},$$
$$(1_{GD}\otimes e')(c'\otimes1_{GD})=G\bigl((1_D\otimes e)(c\otimes1_D)\bigr)=1_{GD}.$$
Each equality is the substitution of the naturality, associativity, and unit equations in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]; no preservation-of-duals theorem is being assumed.

proof.text:
For $N\in\mathcal C$ abbreviate $H_N=H_{\mathcal C}(P,N)$ and $v_N=\operatorname{ev}_{P,N}$. Put
$$a_N=\lambda_N\circ(e\otimes1_N)\circ\alpha^{-1}_{P,D,N}:P\otimes(D\otimes N)\to N,$$
$$\phi_N=\operatorname{curry}(a_N):D\otimes N\to H_N,$$
$$\psi_N=(1_D\otimes v_N)\circ\alpha_{D,P,H_N}\circ(c\otimes1_{H_N})\circ\lambda_{H_N}^{-1}:H_N\to D\otimes N.$$
The inverse-transpose equation of [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] gives $v_N(1_P\otimes\phi_N)=a_N$. Substitute this into $\psi_N\phi_N$ and move $\phi_N$ across the insertion of $c$ by bifunctoriality. Omitting only the indicated structural isomorphisms, this reads
$$\psi_N\phi_N=(1_D\otimes a_N)(c\otimes1_{D\otimes N})=\bigl((1_D\otimes e)(c\otimes1_D)\bigr)\otimes1_N=1_{D\otimes N}.$$
The last equality is the assumed triangle identity for $D$. This computes an explicit inverse composite, rather than assuming an arbitrary identification of internal Hom with dual tensor.

source.place: Tags 0FFP (definition-dual, functoriality immediately following it), 0FFQ (lemma-left-dual, explicit insertion/contraction proof), and 0GWJ (remark-internal-hom-monoidal). Tensor order follows the item; no symmetry is used.

proof.text:
For the other composite use injectivity of the inverse adjunction bijection, with its formula in [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws]. Substitution of $\psi_N$ and the equation $v_N(1_P\otimes\phi_N)=a_N$ gives
$$\operatorname{uncurry}(\phi_N\psi_N)=a_N(1_P\otimes\psi_N)=v_N\circ\bigl(((e\otimes1_P)(1_P\otimes c))\otimes1_{H_N}\bigr)=v_N=\operatorname{uncurry}(1_{H_N}).$$
For the middle equality, both expanded maps insert $c$ between $P$ and $H_N$, giving factors $P,D,P,H_N$; contracting the first two factors by $e$ and the last two by $v_N$ commutes by the tensor bifunctor law. The assumed triangle identity for $P$ then contracts $P,D,P$ to $P$. Hence $\phi_N\psi_N=1_{H_N}$. Together with step 2 this makes $\phi_N$ an isomorphism with inverse $\psi_N$. Repeat exactly these two substitutions in $\mathcal D$, using the triangles verified in step 1: the transpose $\phi'_{GN}:GD\otimes GN\to H_{\mathcal D}(GP,GN)$ of $a'_{GN}=\lambda_{GN}(e'\otimes1_{GN})\alpha^{-1}_{GP,GD,GN}$ is an isomorphism as well.

source.place: Tags 0FFP (definition-dual, functoriality immediately following it), 0FFQ (lemma-left-dual, explicit insertion/contraction proof), and 0GWJ (remark-internal-hom-monoidal). Tensor order follows the item; no symmetry is used.

proof.text:
Compare the two maps $\gamma_{P,N}\circ G(\phi_N)\circ\mu_{D,N}$ and $\phi'_{GN}$ from $GD\otimes GN$ to $H_{\mathcal D}(GP,GN)$. By [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] and the defining transpose of $\gamma$, the inverse transpose of the first map is
$$G(v_N)\circ\mu_{P,H_N}\circ\bigl(1_{GP}\otimes(G(\phi_N)\circ\mu_{D,N})\bigr)
=G(a_N)\circ\mu_{P,D\otimes N}\circ(1_{GP}\otimes\mu_{D,N}).$$
Here tensorator naturality and $v_N(1_P\otimes\phi_N)=a_N$ give the equality. Expand $a_N$ in the right side. Associativity coherence first rewrites it as
$$G(\lambda_N)\circ G(e\otimes1_N)\circ\mu_{P\otimes D,N}\circ(\mu_{P,D}\otimes1_{GN})\circ\alpha^{-1}_{GP,GD,GN}.$$
Naturality changes $G(e\otimes1_N)\mu_{P\otimes D,N}$ to $\mu_{\mathbf1,N}(G(e)\otimes1_{GN})$. Unit coherence says $G(\lambda_N)\mu_{\mathbf1,N}=\lambda_{GN}(u^{-1}\otimes1_{GN})$. Thus the result is precisely $\lambda_{GN}(e'\otimes1_{GN})\alpha^{-1}_{GP,GD,GN}=a'_{GN}$, the inverse transpose of the second map. Injectivity of transposition proves
$$\gamma_{P,N}\circ G(\phi_N)\circ\mu_{D,N}=\phi'_{GN}.$$

source.place: Tags 0FFP (definition-dual, functoriality immediately following it), 0FFQ (lemma-left-dual, explicit insertion/contraction proof), and 0GWJ (remark-internal-hom-monoidal). Tensor order follows the item; no symmetry is used.

proof.text:
Both $\phi_N$ and $\phi'_{GN}$ are isomorphisms by steps 2–3, and $\mu_{D,N}$ is an isomorphism by [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. A functor preserves an explicit two-sided inverse: $G(\phi_N)G(\psi_N)=G(1)=1$ and $G(\psi_N)G(\phi_N)=1$. The equality in step 4 therefore gives
$$\gamma_{P,N}=\phi'_{GN}\circ\mu_{D,N}^{-1}\circ G(\psi_N),$$
with inverse $G(\phi_N)\circ\mu_{D,N}\circ(\phi'_{GN})^{-1}$. This proves invertibility of the specified comparison for every $N$, using only the displayed dual-pair identities and the strong monoidal structure.
